selection_rule: Every statement by an in-scope officeholder quoted in a story published on Nov. 21 or 22, 2026 in the NPR Politics and PBS NewsHour Politics feeds, as read on Nov. 22 at about 08:07 ET, less the stories earlier pages already used, plus every transcript from the fixed transcript sources dated in that window (none was). Transcripts from Nov. 15 to 20 were searched only to confirm quotes. PBS NewsHour carries Associated Press reporting. Two of the eleven stories quoted no officeholder in scope. Greetings and procedural remarks, quotes under five words, commentators' accounts of what officials said, and statements by officials outside the offices in scope were left out. Statements are worded as the outlet reported them; entries beginning "Reported as" are the reporter's wording.
lede: Ten officeholders in scope were quoted in the Nov. 21 and 22 political coverage of NPR and PBS NewsHour, for 28 statements in all. Most came from a White House news conference at which President Trump, Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio recapped Trump's trip to Asia and his meeting with the leaders of China and Russia, and took questions about the Iran war and the 2028 Republican field.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent spoke about export restrictions on Nvidia chips to China and about the Commerce Department's handling of Megaspeed International. Trump spoke in a Fox News Channel interview about the apparent hack of an FBI criminal justice database and about capping credit card interest rates, a proposal Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Josh Hawley have also backed.

Reps. Robert Garcia and Jamie Raskin responded to Trump's order telling federal contractors to check with the White House before answering Congress. Rep. Greg Murphy described how North Carolina's redrawn congressional map changed his district, and Rep. Hakeem Jeffries addressed voters after the midterm elections.

statements.speaker: Greg Murphy
statements.context: Murphy, the Republican congressman for North Carolina's 3rd District, described his district after the Republican-drawn map moved four counties into it.
statements.quote: It made us the weakest Republican district in the state.
statements.test: True if, under the congressional map in force for the 2026 election, North Carolina's 3rd District has the lowest Republican vote share or partisan lean of the state's Republican-leaning districts. False if another Republican-leaning North Carolina district is weaker for Republicans on the same measure. Cannot be determined if no district-level vote or lean data for the new map is available.
statements.finding: Figures attributed to the North Carolina General Assembly, as reported by Roll Call and WFAE (the Assembly's district file could not be read directly), put Trump's 2024 margin in the redrawn 3rd District at about 14 points, down from 22, but about 12 points in the 1st and 10 points in the unchanged 11th. Whether the 3rd is the weakest depends on whether 'Republican district' means seats Republicans held or seats the map leans Republican, and on the measure used.

statements.speaker: Donald Trump
statements.context: Trump, asked at a White House news conference about comparisons of his meeting with the Chinese and Russian leaders to the 1945 Yalta Conference, described his thinking before the trip.
statements.quote: I didn't go having us talk about Yalta, and if you look, Winston Churchill, Stalin, FDR - which was a big one - I didn't think about it.
statements.test: True if records of the trip show no Yalta comparison or agenda item raised by Trump or the White House before or during the trilateral meeting. False if Trump or the White House is on record invoking Yalta before the meeting. Cannot be determined if no record speaks to what Trump planned or thought before the trip.
statements.finding: An Anadolu Agency explainer dated Nov. 18, the day before the meeting, attributes the Yalta comparisons to news outlets, Ukrainian President Zelenskyy and Kremlin spokesman Peskov, not to Trump or the White House. Newsweek reports that Trump called the meeting "bigger than Yalta" and posted a Yalta image only after the meeting. No White House record of the trip could be read directly, and no record shows what Trump thought before the trip.

statements.speaker: Scott Bessent
statements.context: Bessent, the Treasury Secretary, spoke to CNBC after the Asia trip about chip restrictions on China following the administration's move to block China's remote access to advanced chips.
statements.quote: The proper chip restrictions are in place,

statements.speaker: Scott Bessent
statements.context: Bessent, the Treasury Secretary, spoke to CNBC after the Asia trip about Chinese firms' remote access to Nvidia chips.
statements.quote: And the remote access has been curtailed.
statements.test: True if the administration took a published action in November 2026 restricting Chinese firms' remote access to advanced Nvidia chips. False if no such restriction was issued or it was withdrawn. Cannot be determined if only reports of a planned action exist with no official text.
statements.finding: The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security published an interim final rule, "Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors" (2026-23529), in the Federal Register on Nov. 19, 2026. It requires licenses for exports to overseas data centers that remotely supply significant computing power to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other Country Group D:5 nations. No withdrawal was found, and the rule's effective date was not read.

statements.speaker: Scott Bessent
statements.context: AP reported what Bessent said the previous week about the Commerce Department and chip export restrictions on Megaspeed International.
statements.quote: Reported as: Last week, Bessent said he was frustrated with the Commerce Department's delay in placing restrictions on Nvidia chip exports to Megaspeed International, which is under investigation by the U.S. for potentially diverting restricted Nvidia AI chips to China.

source.note: ABC This Week (Nov. 15) carries Bessent saying Treasury, War, USTR and State favored putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months but Commerce has the pen; the word 'frustrated' and the 'rebuke' framing are AP's, not in that transcript.

statements.test: True if, as of mid-November 2026, Megaspeed International had not been added to the Commerce Department's Entity List or otherwise restricted by Commerce. False if Commerce had already placed Megaspeed on the Entity List or imposed export restrictions on it before then. Cannot be determined if the Entity List status and timing cannot be established.
statements.premise: The Commerce Department had not placed export restrictions on Megaspeed International as of mid-November 2026, though Treasury wanted them.
statements.finding: A Federal Register search for Megaspeed returns no documents, and the Commerce Department's 2026 Entity List rules contain no Megaspeed addition, so Commerce had not listed it as of mid-November 2026. On ABC's This Week on Nov. 15, Bessent said Treasury, War, USTR and State had favored listing it for months.

evidence.label: Federal Register: BIS Entity List documents, 2026

statements.speaker: Scott Bessent
statements.context: AP reported what Bessent said about which department controlled export restrictions on Megaspeed International.
statements.quote: Reported as: In an unusually public rebuke of a fellow Cabinet member, Bessent said his department wanted to place export controls on Megaspeed, but Commerce was in charge of the matter.

source.note: ABC This Week (Nov. 15) carries Bessent saying Treasury, War, USTR and State favored putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months but Commerce has the pen; the word 'frustrated' and the 'rebuke' framing are AP's, not in that transcript.

statements.test: True if the Commerce Department (its Bureau of Industry and Security) holds the authority to add companies such as Megaspeed to the Entity List and impose export controls, rather than Treasury. False if Treasury or another department holds that authority. Cannot be determined if the relevant authority cannot be established from primary sources.
statements.finding: The Export Control Reform Act, 50 U.S.C. 4813(a), gives the Secretary of Commerce authority over the export control lists, in consultation with State, Defense and Energy. BIS Entity List rules describe additions as decided by an interagency End-User Review Committee, in which Treasury takes part where appropriate but does not hold the authority.

evidence.label: Federal Register: BIS Entity List rules, 2026

statements.speaker: Donald Trump
statements.context: AP reported what Trump said in a Fox News Channel interview about working with the incoming Democratic Congress on a credit card interest rate cap.
statements.quote: Reported as: President Donald Trump said Saturday that he would work with the incoming Democratic Congress to cap credit card interest rates, hoping to fulfill a promise he made on the 2024 campaign trail but couldn't deliver on because of industry pressure and a lack of interest from his fellow Republicans.

statements.speaker: Donald Trump
statements.context: Trump, in a Fox News Channel interview, spoke about credit card companies while discussing a credit card interest rate cap.
statements.quote: These credit card companies have made a lot
statements.test: True if credit card issuers' profits or interest income are high by official measures (for example Federal Reserve or FDIC data on card-bank returns or card interest income). False if official data show credit card lending was unprofitable or earned unusually little. Cannot be determined if the loose term 'a lot' leaves the data open to more than one reading.
statements.finding: The Federal Reserve's report to Congress on credit card profitability (latest edition read: July 2019, 2018 data) shows large credit card banks earned 3.79% of assets before taxes against 1.46% for all commercial banks, and lost money in only one year (2009) of 2001 to 2018. AskAmerica's data show the commercial bank credit card interest rate at about 21% from 2023 through August 2026 (21.19% latest), but no official profitability figure after 2018 was read.

evidence.label: econ.fred_indicators (card interest rate TERMCBCCALLNS and charge-off rate CORCCACBS, 2023 to 2026)
evidence.sql: SELECT series, "date", "value" FROM econ.fred_indicators WHERE series IN ('TERMCBCCALLNS','CORCCACBS') AND "date" >= '2023-01-01' ORDER BY series, "date"

evidence.label: Federal Reserve, Profitability of Credit Card Operations of Depository Institutions (July 2019)

statements.speaker: Elizabeth Warren
statements.context: Warren, a Democratic senator expected to chair the Senate Banking Committee, responded to Trump's Fox News interview on capping credit card interest rates.
statements.quote: Let's cap credit card interest rates and save Americans money.

statements.speaker: Josh Hawley
statements.context: Hawley, a Republican senator, spoke about his bill to cap credit card interest rates when Trump proposed a cap earlier this year.
statements.quote: Congress should pass my bipartisan bill to cap these rates and deliver relief right away,
statements.test: True if Congress's records show a bill sponsored by Hawley to cap credit card interest rates with at least one cosponsor from the other party. False if Hawley has no such bill, or his bill has no cosponsor from the other party. Cannot be determined if bill records are unavailable.
statements.premise: Hawley has introduced a bipartisan bill to cap credit card interest rates.
statements.finding: Congress's bill records show Hawley sponsored S. 2760 in the 118th Congress, a credit card rate cap with no cosponsors. In the 119th Congress he is a cosponsor, added the day it was introduced (Feb. 4, 2025), of S. 381, the 10 Percent Credit Card Interest Rate Cap Act sponsored by Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), whose other cosponsors are Democrats Merkley and Gillibrand. Whether "my bipartisan bill" fits a bill he cosponsors rather than sponsors is a question of wording the records do not settle.

evidence.label: law.bills (Hawley-sponsored credit card and interest-rate bills)
evidence.sql: SELECT congress, bill_type, bill_number, title, sponsor_full_name, sponsor_party, cosponsor_count, latest_action_text FROM law.bills WHERE sponsor_full_name LIKE '%Hawley%' AND (LOWER(title) LIKE '%interest%' OR LOWER(title) LIKE '%credit card%')

evidence.label: law.bills (119th Congress credit card and interest-rate bills)
evidence.sql: SELECT congress, bill_type, bill_number, title, sponsor_full_name, cosponsor_count, introduced_date, latest_action_text FROM law.bills WHERE congress=119 AND (LOWER(title) LIKE '%credit card%' OR LOWER(title) LIKE '%interest rate%') ORDER BY bill_type, bill_number

evidence.label: law.bill_cosponsors (S. 381, 119th Congress)
evidence.sql: SELECT bill_number, full_name, sponsorship_date, is_original_cosponsor, withdrawn_date FROM law.bill_cosponsors WHERE congress=119 AND bill_type='s' AND bill_number=381
